title: Blackcurrant plate pie
subtitle: A double-crust fruit pie made in a deep pie plate with sharp blackcurrant filling
excerpt: A blackcurrant plate pie has pastry above and below the fruit, baked in a deep ceramic plate rather than a tin. The blackcurrants give a sharp, intensely flavoured filling that balances the buttery pastry. Cornflour thickens the juices so the pie cuts cleanly rather than flooding the plate when sliced.
sourceNotes: Plate pies are a traditional British form distinct from deep-dish pies: made in a ceramic or enamel plate, shallower, with a higher pastry-to-fruit ratio. Blackcurrant is a classic British filling suited to the sharp-fruit style documented across home-baking and preserving literature.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked with the pastry lid on. Bake from frozen at 190 degrees Celsius for 55 to 60 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Fill and top the pie up to 24 hours ahead and keep refrigerated unbaked. Bake from cold, adding 5 to 10 minutes.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 190 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 175 degrees Celsius. Middle shelf. Start at the higher temperature to crisp the pastry, then reduce if the top colours too quickly.

glossaryTerms.definition: A double-crust pie baked in a shallow ceramic or enamel plate rather than a deep tin. The plate shape gives a shallower pie with a high proportion of pastry to fruit. The pastry base sits directly on the plate and absorbs some fruit juice during baking, giving a softer base than a tin-baked pie.

content.text: needs more sugar than a plate pie made with sweeter fruit, and it needs the cornflour thickening or the juices will flood the pie when cut. Use a deep ceramic plate rather than a metal one; it absorbs heat more gently and the pastry base is less likely to burn before the lid is golden.

items.prepNote: fresh or frozen (no need to thaw)

content.text: Rub the cold butter into the flour and icing sugar until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Mix in the egg yolk and enough cold water to bring the dough together without kneading. Divide in two (one slightly larger piece for the base). Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Toss the blackcurrants with the caster sugar and cornflour. Leave for 10 minutes; the sugar will draw out some juice.

Using a rolling pin, roll the larger piece of pastry to a round and use it to line a 23 cm deep ceramic pie plate, leaving about 2 cm overhanging the rim. Pile the blackcurrant mixture in, mounding it slightly in the centre.

Roll the second piece of pastry into a round for the lid. Brush the overhanging pastry edge with egg wash. Lay the lid over the filling and press the edges together to seal. Trim and crimp. Cut two small slits in the lid to allow steam to escape.
Brush the lid with egg wash and scatter caster sugar over it. Bake at 190 degrees Celsius for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden. Cool for at least 20 minutes before slicing.
